title: Father's early bands: Excelsior brass band and Robichaux, with associates
summary: His father's start at 11 or 12, the old brass band, and Crusto, Boasso, Gaspard, Fields, Elgar, Chandler and Mac Murray.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: This feels about over. There's another minute or two, if there's anything else we can think of about your father and we're getting into your life. For instance, do you know how old he was when this other boy began helping him with the drums?
And did he ever tell you about his first jobs or the first bands he played with? You mentioned Robichaux for one.

Robichaux is one of the bands that I do remember him speaking of as an orchestra. But you take way back was the old Excelsa band, which was not of the group in later years. I think it was the original band was Tio and Dublé band. And then it went into the name of Excelsa band. Was that Brass Band mostly?
Oh, it was Brass Band. Of course, the Brass Band in that area, they would play for outdoor parties and everything else during that time. That's what I've heard they play for dancing even.

That was a man made up of I think some of Mineta's relatives, some of his older group. Some names that I don't even remember. Another name that I can't recall of was Crusto. He was a trumpet player. I think he was the one that had taught Perez if I'm not mistaken. Crusto and then there's a fellow by the name of Boasso. He was the old baritone in the area. I also worked with the old, well they were about in the same area. Like Vic Gasper and his brother. Yes. Old Gasper. George Fields. He was, I think he's dead just about five or six years now.

No, no. Another father he played with was Charles Elgar. I knew him. He's still up there. He's an officer in the union. He's vice president. He's vice president. Many years. They were just about the same age. My father might be one or two years older than he. A fellow by the name of Ralph Marniegu. That was another one in that old brass band in that area. Ralph Marniegu. That was a soldier. Who I saw. I heard him mention out. I said Crusto. That's the name. Diddy Chandler. Diddy Chandler came up right around in the same area. With my father. I'll often know him speak of me and Mac Murray.

Oh yes. We never didn't know much about Mac Murray. You happen to know what his real name... Some people say his first name was Mac and his last name Murray? No, that was his last name. His last name was Mac Murray. Now, I'm trying to think what was his first name.

I can't recall, but that was his last name. Paul Barber and maybe thought his name was John Mac Murray. I think it was John Mac Murray. I'm not sure. I'm not sure, but Mac Murray was his... Was his whole name when big names. Yeah, it was his last name.
Do you remember anything about John Veen? Oh, yes. I can remember John Veen. His son is up now.
